Rashi on Niddah 58a:10:1.hebrew: עד היכא - קרוי פנים מעובי השוק, ולא אמרינן צדדין נינהו:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:10:1.english: Until where - Is it called "the inside" of the thickness of the leg, and we do not say that they are sides?

Rashi on Niddah 58a:10:2.hebrew: עד מקום חבק - ספק. וכמדומה לי שהוא קפץ הירך והשוק, שקורין יירי"ט, וקאמר: עד מקום שהוא מתחיל קרוי פנים. וחבק היא מתיחת הגידין שחובקין הירך והשוק יחד סמוך לאותו קפץ, כמו (שבת דף סד.) את הקילקי ואת החבק:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:10:2.english: Until the place of the ḥavak - [This is in] doubt. And it seems to me that it is the bend of the thigh and the leg, which is called jarret [in Old French]; and [the Gemara] is saying: Up to the place where it begins, it is called the inner side. And ḥavak is the extension of the tendons that clasp the thigh and the leg together near that bend, as in (Shabbat 64a): "the kilki and the ḥavak" [reins and a saddle band].

Rashi on Niddah 58a:12:1.english: Like a bracelet - A strip in a circle, like a bracelet.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:12:2.english: What is [the halakha] - Do we hold it in doubt [whether it is] the blood of a niddah, or not?

Rashi on Niddah 58a:13:1.hebrew: כרצועה - לאורך הירך, דהיינו אורחיה, כשנופל ושותת נעשה כרצועה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:13:1.english: Like a strip - Along the length of the thigh, which is its usual way, as when [blood] falls and flows, it becomes like a strip.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:14:1.hebrew: במשתיתא - עם המסכת דשמשון (שופטים טז) מתרגמינן עם משתיתא. שהיתה מסכת טווי לאריג, ונמצא דם על השתי:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:14:1.english: In the warp - [The phrase] "with the web" in [the story of] Samson (Judges 16) is translated [in the Targum as] "with the warp." [Meaning] that there was a web of spun thread for weaving, and blood was found on the warp.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:14:2.hebrew: תיזיל ותיתי - כדרך שעשתה עד עכשיו, שהלכה ושבה. אי מתרמי שהטווי המוסך, שקורין אורדי"ר, בא בין רגליה כנגד אותו מקום, טמאה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:14:2.english: Let her go and come - In the manner that she did until now, as she walked back and forth. If it happens that the warped yarn, which is called ourdir [to warp], comes between her legs opposite that place [her pudenda], she is ritually impure.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:15:1.hebrew: והתניא אין שונין בטהרות - גבי מתעטף בטליתו וטהרות וטמאות בצדו בפ"ק (לעיל נדה דף ה:): ספק נגע ספק לא נגע, טהור. ואם אי אפשר אא"כ נגע, טמא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר: אע"פ דלא אפשר, לא מטמינן ליה, אלא אומרים לו: שנה, ואי לא נגע, מטהרינן ליה. אמרו לו: אין שונין בטהרות, דאף על גב דהשתא לא מיתרמי, דלמא מעיקרא לא הוה הכי:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:15:1.english: But isn't it taught: One does not repeat in matters of purity - Regarding [one who] wraps himself in his cloak, and pure and impure [items] are beside him, in the first chapter (above, Niddah 5b): [If there is] uncertainty whether he touched or uncertainty whether he did not touch, [it is] pure; and if it is impossible unless he touched, [it is] impure. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Even though it is impossible [not to have touched], we do not declare him impure; rather, we say to him: "Repeat [the action]," and if he does not touch [them], we declare him pure. They said to him: "One does not repeat in matters of purity," for even though now it did not happen [to touch], perhaps initially it was not so.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:15:2.hebrew: כי אמרינן אין שונין לקולא - כגון בההיא דא"א לו אא"כ נגע וטמא, ואנן ניקו ונימא ליה שנה להקל. אבל הכא חומרא הוא, דמסתמא טהורה, דהא לא על בשרה ולא על חלוקה אשתכח; והאי דאמר תיזיל ותיתי, ואי מתרמי מטמינן לה — חומרא היא:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:15:2.english: When we say that one does not repeat, [it is] to be lenient - For example, in that [case] where it is impossible for him [to wrap himself] unless he touched [the impurity], and [thus he is] impure, and shall we go and say to him, "Repeat," to be lenient? But here it is a stringency, for presumably she is pure, since [the blood] was found neither on her flesh nor on her shift; and this that [Rabbi Yannai] said, "Let her go and come," so that if it happens [that the warp reaches between her legs] we declare her impure, is a stringency.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:16:1.english: This matter - [In the mishna:] "She would remove it and cover herself with it at night, etc."

Rashi on Niddah 58a:17:1.hebrew: חלוקה של קצרה - ולא בדקתו קודם לבישה, ואחר כך נמצא עליו דם:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:17:1.english: The robe of a short woman - And she did not examine it before wearing [it], and afterward blood was found upon it.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:17:2.english: If it reaches - [That is, the] stain.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:17:3.hebrew: כנגד בית התורפה של ארוכה - טמאה אף ארוכה, וכ"ש קצרה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:17:3.english: Opposite the pudenda of the tall woman - The tall woman too is ritually impure, and all the more so the short woman.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:17:4.hebrew: ואם לאו טהורה הארוכה - אבל קצרה טמאה, שהרי כנגד בית התורפה שלה הוא מגיע:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:17:4.english: And if not, the tall [woman] is pure - But the short [woman] is impure, for it reaches opposite her pudenda.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:18:2.hebrew: ולענין דינא - דכבוס הכתם מן החלוק תנן דחבירתה תולה בה, דאמרה אחרונה: לא מהימנת לי דאת בדקתיה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:18:2.english: And with regard to judgment - [Regarding] the laundering of the stain from the robe, we learned that her friend may attribute [it] to her, as the latter says: "You are not credible to me that you examined it."

Rashi on Niddah 58a:1:1.english: By rabbinic law - Perhaps she sensed [the emission], but was unaware of it.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:2:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - טעמא דשמואל דאמר לעיל בדקה קרקע עולם כו', לאו משום הרגשה, אלא כרבי נחמיה ס"ל, דאמר: לא הזכירו חכמים גזרת כתם אלא על דבר המקבל טומאה. הלכך, כל הנך תיובתא לאו קושיא נינהו, דשמואל לא איירי בהרגשה כלל:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:2:1.english: Rav Ashi said - The reason of Samuel, who said above: "[If] she checked the ground of the world..." etc., is not due to sensation, but rather he holds in accordance with Rabbi Nechemya, who said: "The Sages did not mention the decree of a stain except upon an object that is susceptible to ritual impurity." Therefore, all those refutations are not difficulties, for Samuel was not dealing with sensation at all.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:3:1.hebrew: אלא רב ירמיה מדפתי - דקבלה לתיובתא דלעיל, ושני: מודה שמואל כו'. ומדקבלה לתיובתא, מכלל דטעמא דשמואל משום הרגשה. ואי משום הרגשה, מאי איריא קרקע? אפילו גלימא נמי: בדקה בטלית וישבה עליה, ואחר כך מצאה דם – טהורה, שלא הרגישה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:3:1.english: Rather, Rav Yirmeya of Difti - For he accepted the objection above, and answered: "Shmuel concedes [that she is impure rabbinically], etc." And since he accepted the objection, it follows that Shmuel's reason is because of sensation. And if [his reason is] because of sensation, why specifically ground? Even [on] a cloak as well: [if] she examined a cloak, sat upon it, and afterwards found blood, [she should be] pure, since she did not sense.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:6:1.hebrew: בצוארה - אם נמצא דם כנגד תורפה, יכולה לתלות במכה של צוארה, שפעמים שמטה את צוארה לפניה ונופל דם המכה על תחתית חלוקה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:6:1.english: On her neck - If blood is found opposite her private parts, she can attribute [it] to the wound on her neck, for sometimes she bends her neck forward and the blood of the wound falls onto the bottom of her robe.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:6:2.hebrew: על כתפה שאינה יכולה לתלות - שאין דם בא מכתפה ונופל לפניה, אין תולה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:6:2.english: On her shoulder, where she cannot attribute [it] - Since blood does not come from her shoulder and fall in front of her, she may not attribute [it].

Rashi on Niddah 58a:7:1.english: And we do not say she took it with her hand - From the wound on her shoulder and brought it in front of her.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:7:2.hebrew: עביד דמתרמי - תחת אותו מקום, ודם נוטף עליו:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:7:2.english: It is prone to happen - [That it comes] beneath that place, and blood drips upon it.

Rashi on Niddah 58a:8:1.hebrew: על קשרי אצבעותיה - היינו גב היד. והא גב היד, אפילו בשעת בדיקה לא נגעה, מ"ט טמאה:
Rashi on Niddah 58a:8:1.english: On the joints of her fingers - That is the back of the hand. And behold, the back of the hand does not touch even at the time of examination; what is the reason she is impure?

Rashi on Niddah 58a:9:1.english: Is it not because we say that she examined with the other hand and [it] touched - The hand that examined [touched] the back of its fellow [hand].

Tosafot on Niddah 58a:10:1.hebrew: מקום חבק - פרש"י שהוא קפץ הירך והשוק, וחבק הוא מקום מתיחת הגידים שחובקים הירך והשוק. ובערוך פירש שנועלין אנפליאות שיש בה לולאות, ומקום חבור הלולאות קרי חבק. ועוד פירש פירוש אחר: שכופף השוק על הירך, מה שמתכסה הבשר ע"י כפיפת השוק על ירך, שחובקין זה את זה, קרי מקום חבק:
Tosafot on Niddah 58a:10:1.english: The place of clasping - Rashi explained that it is the bend of the thigh and the leg, and ḥavak is the place of the stretching of the tendons that clasp the thigh and the leg. And in the Arukh he explained that they wear slippers that have loops, and the place where the loops join is called ḥavak. And he further explained another interpretation: that when one bends the leg against the thigh, the flesh that is covered by means of the bending of the leg against the thigh, as they clasp each other, is called the place of ḥavak.

Tosafot on Niddah 58a:12:1.hebrew: כשורה מהו - אומר ר"י דהיינו טיפין טיפין, דאי מחוברת השורה יחד, היינו רצועה דבסמוך. וטיפין טיפין היינו מעורבבין, שאינו לא כשיר ולא כשורה. והא דאמר לקמן טיפין טיפין אין מצטרפין, היינו על הבגד; והכא מיירי על בשרה, דיש יותר לתלות בדם מאכולת על הבגד מעל בשרה:
Tosafot on Niddah 58a:12:1.english: [If it is] like a row, what is [the halakha]? - Ri says that this means [separate] drops; for if the row were connected together, that would be [the case of] a strip (retzu'ah) [mentioned] nearby. And [the case of] "drops [and] drops" means [drops that are] scattered, which is neither like a bracelet nor like a row. And that which is stated later on, that "drops [and] drops do not combine," that is on a garment; whereas here it is dealing with [blood found] on her flesh, as there is more [reason] to attribute [a stain] to the blood of a louse on a garment than on her flesh.

Tosafot on Niddah 58a:18:1.hebrew: ולענין דינא תנן - וא"ת, מדינא נמי תתחייב השניה לכבסו, כדאמר בהמדיר (כתובות עו:), כל שנולד ספק ברשותו עליו להביא ראיה? וי"ל, כיון דאינה לשניה אלא בתורת שאלה, אינה ממש ברשותה. ועוד יש לומר, דהתם קאמר שאם ירצה להוציא יביא ראיה; אבל הכא, לא תתחייב האחרונה לכבסו:
Tosafot on Niddah 58a:18:1.english: And with regard to [monetary] law we learned - And if you say: According to the law as well, let the second [woman] be obligated to launder it, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] HaMaddir (Ketubot 76b): "Whoever in whose domain an uncertainty arose, upon him is [the burden] to bring proof"? And one can say: Since [the robe] is in the possession of the second [woman] only by way of a loan, it is not truly in her domain. And furthermore, one can say that there it means that if he wishes to extract [payment], he must bring proof; but here, the latter [woman] cannot be obligated to launder it.

Tosafot on Niddah 58a:2:1.hebrew: כרבי נחמיה דאמר כל דבר שאינו מקבל טומאה כו' - טעמא דרבי נחמיה: כיון דדבר שהכתם בו טהור, גם על האשה לא גזרו טומאה. וההיא משתיתא דבסמוך, נהי דלא מקבלה טומאה, מ"מ מקבל טומאה בנגעים:
Tosafot on Niddah 58a:2:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Neḥemya, who said: Any item that is not susceptible to ritual impurity, etc. - The reason of Rabbi Neḥemya [is that] since the item on which the stain [is found] is ritually pure, they did not decree ritual impurity upon the woman either. And that warp [mentioned] nearby: Although it is not susceptible to [standard] ritual impurity, nevertheless it is susceptible to ritual impurity through [tzara'at] afflictions.

Tosafot on Niddah 58a:5:1.hebrew: ומי מחזקינן טומאה ממקום למקום - וקשה, דמאי פריך? דודאי להקל לא מחזקינן, אבל להחמיר כי הכא מחמרינן, דהכי אמר לקמן: אין שונין בטהרות להקל, אבל לחומרא שונין. ויש לומר: כיון דכתמים דרבנן, אי איתא דתלינן להחמיר, להקל נמי היה לנו לתלות בדבר הרגיל קצת; אבל לענין ממקום למקום שאין רגילות כל כך, אמרינן לקמן בסמוך דאפילו בכתמים שונין לחומרא ולא להקל. תימה, דליפרוך ממתניתין: שלא כנגד התורפה טהורה, ולא אמר: בדקה בהאי ידא ונגעה בבשרה למעלה מן התורפה! וי"ל, דאם איתא דבדקה ומצאה טמאה, היתה זכורה והויא רמיא אדעתה שהיא טמאה; אבל כי נגעה בדם שעל כתפה, לא רמיא אנפשה, כיון דאין זה דם טמא. ובסמוך גבי דם טמא דפריך: ואימא דבדקה בהאי ידא ונגעה באידך — פריך מכ"ש, וממתניתין נמי הוה מצי למפרך. ויש לחלק בין ממקום למקום דהכא לההוא דפ"ק (לעיל נדה דף ד.): דהתם טומאה עצמה באה ממקום למקום, והכא טומאה עצמה במקום אחד עומדת:
Tosafot on Niddah 58a:5:1.english: And do we presume ritual impurity [moves] from place to place? - And it is difficult: What is [the Gemara's] question? For certainly to be lenient we do not establish a presumption [that impurity moved], but to be stringent, like here, we should be stringent! For so [the Gemara] says below (58a): "One does not repeat [actions] in [matters of] purities to be lenient, but for stringency one does repeat." And one can say: Since [the laws of] stains are rabbinic, if it were so that we attribute [transfer] to be stringent, we also should have attributed [it] to be lenient in a matter that is somewhat common. But with regard to [transfer] from place to place, which is not so common, [we do not do so, whereas] we say shortly below that even regarding stains one repeats [an action] for stringency and not for leniency. [It is] astonishing: Let [the Gemara] challenge from our Mishnah: "[If she saw blood on her flesh] not opposite the pudenda (ha-turpa), she is pure" — and [the Tanna] does not say [she is impure because] she examined [herself] with this hand and touched her flesh above the pudenda! And one can say: If it were so that she examined [herself] and found [blood, rendering her] impure, she would have remembered, and it would have been on her mind that she is impure. But when she touched the blood that was on her shoulder, she would not pay attention [to it], since this is not impure blood. And shortly below [58a:9], regarding impure blood, where [the Gemara] challenges: "And say that she examined with this hand and touched the other [hand]?" — it challenges *a fortiori*; and from our Mishnah, too, it could have challenged. And one can differentiate between [presuming transfer] "from place to place" here and that of the first chapter (above, Niddah 4a): For there, the ritual impurity itself traveled from place to place, whereas here, the ritual impurity itself remains in one place.
